subject: SLA baseline uplift request — monthly remedy phasing & carveouts
messages:
From: Anna Kim <anna.kim@luminarai.com>
To: marissa_cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: procurement@luminarai.com
Date: Mon, 01 Jun 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: SLA baseline & monthly remedy — initial ask

Hi Marissa,

Thanks again for the demo last week. Procurement is kicking off the contract review and we have a couple of requests we wanted to surface early so we can align with legal and product before the redlines stage. High level:

- Baseline uptime: Luminar needs a 99.95% monthly availability commitment for our production inference endpoints.
- Monthly remedy: we understand credits are per-incident or aggregate; procurement is asking for a monthly cap at 30% of the monthly fee in the first 6 months and a step-down thereafter.
- Onboarding variance: during the first 60–90 days we expect heavier KV cache warmup traffic and some rollout instability; we want a temporary exception window for any availability dips caused by onboarding activities.
- Maintenance carveouts: we propose a maximum 8-hour monthly maintenance window for planned platform upgrades and that maintenance outside of a published window requires 72-hour notice and business approval.

I've attached a short RFI with our preferred phrasing and a sample traffic profile from our staging runs (initial_onboarding_traffic.csv). Can you confirm whether Redwood has a standard proposal that accommodates a phased remedy cap and a time-limited onboarding exception?

If helpful, procurement can run a short call with your CS/Eng to walk the traffic profile and identify where uptime measurements differ for our critical endpoints.

Best,
Anna Kim
Head of Procurement — Luminar AI

Attachment: Luminar_SLA_RFI.pdf
Attachment: initial_onboarding_traffic.csv

From: marissa_cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Anna Kim <anna.kim@luminarai.com>
Cc: ben_carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>, monica_patel <monica.patel@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 01 Jun 2026 13:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: SLA baseline & monthly remedy — initial ask

Hi Anna — thanks for the clear summary and the attachments. Appreciate the heads up on expected staging behavior. A few quick points from our side:

1) Baseline availability: our standard hosted SLA is 99.9% for the full platform. We can offer a path to 99.95% for the specific "inference-critical" endpoints you identify, contingent on traffic shaping and pinned capacity during peak windows (we usually map those into a dedicated pool).

2) Monthly remedy cap: we typically cap aggregated monthly credits at 25% of the monthly invoice for new accounts, with an escalation path that relaxes to 30% for the first 90 days if we jointly agree to an onboarding schedule and runbook. We can formalize a staggered cap (30% first 90 days, 20% months 4–6, 10% thereafter), but need to align on measurement windows and what triggers a credit.

3) Onboarding exception: happy to include a time-boxed exception for "onboarding-induced degradation" — recommended approach is a jointly-signed onboarding runbook with objective checklists (KV warmup, model pinning, traffic ramp steps) and a maximum 90-day window. Any outages during that window would be reviewed against the runbook to determine credit eligibility.

4) Maintenance carveouts: 8-hour monthly planned maintenance is reasonable. We also propose a 1-hour emergency patch carveout with post-facto notice if we need an immediate security fix. 72-hour notice for non-emergency maintenance is standard.

Next steps: I'll pull together a draft amendment to our standard SLA language capturing the phased remedy cap, onboarding exception criteria, and the pinned-endpoint uplift. Looping Ben (AE) and Monica (CS) to confirm the commercial phasing and to propose a short technical call with Neha from our Customer Engineering team to review the traffic CSV.

Thanks —
Marissa Cole
Director, Sales — Redwood Inference

PS: See initial draft here: https://drive.redwood.example.com/teams/sales/luminar/sla-draft-v1
Attachment referenced: none

Folks — forwarding Luminar's RFI. Key asks to triage:

- Procurement wants 99.95% for production inference endpoints and a phased monthly remedy cap that starts at 30% for onboarding.
- They expect a 60–90 day onboarding exception window tied to elevated cache warmup traffic.
- Maintenance carveout: 8 hours / month, 72-hour notice outside of emergencies.

Can you each review and comment inline by EOD PDT?

Monica — confirm commercial acceptance of the proposed stair-step cap (30% → 20% → 10%) and whether we need a minimum commitment to enable 99.95% SLA for specific endpoints.
Ben — any concerns on deal economics if we accept 30% cap for 90 days? Also confirm if we should require a minimum reserved capacity commitment.
Neha — can you take a quick look at the attached traffic CSV and advise whether the onboarding profile materially increases the probability of transient availability dips that would be out-of-scope under our standard SLA? If so, what instrumentation/runbook items would make the exception claimable vs. chargeable?

Thanks —
Marissa

Marissa — thanks for the fast reply and the stair-step proposal. A few clarifying points from Luminar's side before we set the technical call:

- The 99.95% commitment is critical for our SLA to downstream customers; we can agree to a technical annex that pins the two production endpoints that will carry that guarantee. We'll need confirmation on what "pinned capacity" looks like (dedicated pool size) and the requirement to notify us 30 days before any capacity changes.
- We're open to a staggered monthly remedial cap, but prefer 30% for the first 120 days instead of 90 to cover the longer integration tests we run. Could Redwood extend the initial elevated cap to 120 days if we agree to a startup runbook and weekly syncs?
- Latency SLO: We also want a tight latency objective for our critical inference endpoint (p50 < 50ms, p95 < 200ms). If incidents are latency-related (degraded p95), Luminar expects the same crediting treatment as availability incidents for the first 6 months.

If you can incorporate the 120-day window and include the latency objectives in the annex as an optional remedial trigger, we'll be ready to schedule a signatures/ops call next week.

Tom Ellis
VP, Platform Operations — Luminar AI
